author: Michal238
text:
Hi BH.

I have set order when I saw that price is compressing towards my zone. I
 used to set PO without looking at approach when price is retracing
after FL engulf and RR is good. I won't do this though until my PAZ
understanding and MPL understanding will be perfect. Sometimes I was
stopped out, because price did a FO higher than I expected, or I marked
engulf wrong etc. CP is enough for me to set an order. If there is no
CP, and LTF flag is formed bolow my entry point I'll wait till its
engulfed, and then entry on retrace. There are really many scenarios and
 I'll be posting many examples for sure.

author: Michal238
text:
My goal for next few weeks is to find setups I will trade in live
market. I'll have a check list that will help me to stick to my plan.

I'll master each of this setup and I'll ONLY trade what I know that
works and I know how to manage it. I want to improve win ratio

and, most of all be able to exit my trade without any doubt when
reaction is not good enough. Emotional attachment to trades is really

terrible thing.

Also I give up temporarily extra tight SL trades. I want to know that
I'm able to make consistent profits, and having much more winers than
losers is my goal now.

Even if they are small account will grow.

In my price reading I'm going to analyse every turn in the market - if I
 find good zone that didn't work I'll always analyse it in M1 detail on
approach and reaction. By now

I more focused on zones that worked well - and this is a reason why I
have hard time to exit when it is not too late - with smaller loss than
my SL , BE, or even small profit.

Here is setup 1 (perfect example):

It is basicly a QM settup. What I want to highlight here is clear FL and
 engulf of it after reaction to nice demand. If LL reached extreme
orders then I put SL below demand. If not - I put SL below FL, because
price may reach extreme orders in FL.

Exit scenarios. I'll watch PA on approach to blue boxes.

1.

2.

If IT's want to reverse price we will see CP on approach or there will
be a flag formed below supply. I'm not going to exit before limit of
this flag is engulfed.

Difficult thing may be exiting on retrace - not instantly after engulf.
That is one reason why I going to MASTER this setup and see how often I
can exit on retrace.

We know that when there is engulf of FL then price can retrace even
beyond opposite FL. I'm going to find many examples of this scenario and
 see how deep this retrace can be, when price does a FO and where FO
stops. FO can be anticipated when we have fresh level/ DP to engulf
below FL.

Here is one example I found on EURAUD:

Another example is in my post #150.

I'll spend some time mastering this setup. There can be really many
variables of it. It is one setup but once mastered there will be many
opportunities to profit

from it. What I showed above is QM setup it can be also a diamond, can
can. I've put it in context and described briefly how to manage it. I
also have better idea

on elements I must work on. For example - continuation engulf showed in last diagram.

author: Michal238
text:
I agree with Eurotrash. I wouldn't set a PO in this place especially if it is mid-range setup like this one.

If price is moving fast into the zone it won't turn immediately as IT's
have to fill orders, so most of the time we well have opportunity to
enter a trade

after eng on retrace in LTF somtimes with better RR. What is more
important than RR is that in this way you increase probability.

AUDUSD trade was at extreme, and offered really good RR. DP that was
located on edge of CP was in very good place - just above recent highs -
 perfect for FO,

and on RS flip so precise reaction at this level could be expected.

SWAP/RS edit: it is M5
